events.text: Fish and Wildlife Service records give December 21, 1948 as the establishment date of Rabb Lake National Wildlife Refuge, a limited-interest (easement) refuge, under the Act of August 14, 1946, the forerunner of the Fish and Wildlife Coordination Act.

events.note: Pass A found the date only in the FWS limited-interest refuges CCP (Table 4). Pass B found no independent record: no executive order or proclamation for this refuge appears in the National Archives disposition tables (1937-1952) or on the American Presidency Project, and it is not among the North Dakota refuges renamed by Proclamation 2416 in 1940. FWS narrative reports for "North Dakota Easement Refuges" from 1945-1947 suggest the easements predate 1948, so the 1948 date may record a later administrative designation rather than the first protection. Needs a non-FWS source (Federal Register, Interior order, or county easement deed).

rabb-lake-national-wildlife-refuge.note: Limited-interest refuge on private land; establishment date rests on one FWS source.

events.text: The Interior Department established the UL Bend National Wildlife Refuge in Montana by Public Land Order 4588, dated March 25, 1969, which withdrew the lands from the Fort Peck Game Range for the refuge.

authority.citation: Public Land Order 4588 (34 FR 5851), revoking in part Executive Order 7509

sources.name: Federal Register, vol. 34, no. 60 (Mar. 28, 1969), Public Land Order 4588, "Establishment of the UL Bend National Wildlife Refuge"
FWS, CCP: Charles M. Russell and UL Bend NWRs (2012), chronology
FWS ServCat, Establishment Documents: PLO 4588

events.note: Pass A (2012 CCP chronology: PLO 4588 of 03/25/1969 designated the refuge) and Pass B (PLO text in the Federal Register of March 28, 1969, titled "Establishment of the UL Bend National Wildlife Refuge," signed by the Acting Secretary of the Interior and dated March 25, 1969) agree. The FWS ServCat record misdates the PLO as May 25, 1969 in one field.

events.text: The Migratory Bird Conservation Commission approved the UL Bend refuge on February 7, 1967, before the 1969 land order formally established it.

sources.name: FWS, CCP: Charles M. Russell and UL Bend NWRs (2012), chronology

events.note: FWS-only source (the CCP chronology; fws.gov also says "established in 1967"). No Commission report or other independent record was checked.

ul-bend-national-wildlife-refuge.note: FWS dates the refuge to 1967 (Commission approval); the formal land order establishing it is 1969.

events.text: Under a November 26, 1948 agreement with the Truckee-Carson Irrigation District and the Nevada fish and game board, the Fish and Wildlife Service designated the Stillwater National Wildlife Refuge in a notice dated October 17, 1949, effective on publication in the Federal Register on October 21, 1949.

authority.citation: FWS designation under the Act of March 10, 1934, as amended Aug. 14, 1946 (14 FR 6449)

sources.name: Federal Register, vol. 14 (Oct. 21, 1949), p. 6449-6450, "Designation of the Stillwater National Wildlife Refuge"
FWS ServCat, Establishment Documents: Cooperative Agreement (26 Nov 1948) and 14 FR 6449
FWS, Stillwater NWR page

events.note: Pass A (FWS: established in 1949; Realty records the 1948 agreement and the 1949 Federal Register notice) and Pass B (notice text in the Federal Register, signed by Acting Director M. C. James on October 17, 1949, effective on publication, October 21, 1949) agree. The Federal Register notice was written by the Fish and Wildlife Service but is the official published designation.

events.text: Secretary of the Interior Fred A. Seaton's Order 2843 of November 17, 1959 transferred about 4,357 acres of the San Joaquin land utilization project in Tulare County to the Bureau of Sport Fisheries and Wildlife, to be administered as the Pixley National Wildlife Refuge.

authority.citation: Secretary of the Interior Order 2843 (24 FR 9488-9489)

sources.name: Federal Register, vol. 24 (Nov. 25, 1959), p. 9488-9489, Order 2843
FWS ServCat, Establishment Documents: Secretarial Order 2843 (17 Nov 1959)
FWS, Kern and Pixley NWRs Final CCP (2005)

events.note: Pass A (FWS Realty record and 2005 CCP: Secretarial Order 2843 dated November 17, 1959) and Pass B (order text in the Federal Register of November 25, 1959: lands "will be administered as the Pixley National Wildlife Refuge") agree. The order's date line was not legible in the scanned issue, so November 17 rests on the FWS records; fws.gov says the establishment was announced November 20, 1959. Secretary Seaton is named on fws.gov; the order number is confirmed by the Federal Register.

events.name: San Juan National Wildlife Refuge
events.text: The Interior Department established the San Juan National Wildlife Refuge on small islands and rocks in the San Juan Islands by Public Land Order 2249, dated December 24, 1960.

sources.name: Federal Register (Jan. 10, 1961), Public Land Order 2249, "Establishing San Juan National Wildlife Refuge," dated December 24, 1960
FWS ServCat, Establishment Documents: PLO 2249 (24 Dec 1960)
FWS, San Juan Islands NWR page

events.note: Pass A (FWS: established in 1960; Realty record of PLO 2249 dated December 24, 1960) and Pass B (PLO text in the Federal Register of January 10, 1961, titled "Establishing San Juan National Wildlife Refuge," dated December 24, 1960) agree. The same order enlarged the Jones Island Migratory Bird Refuge, set up by Executive Order 7594 of March 30, 1937; that refuge and the Matia Island refuge (EO 7595, also March 30, 1937) were later folded into today's San Juan Islands NWR, but those earlier links were not traced in full here.

san-juan-islands-national-wildlife-refug.note: Today's San Juan Islands NWR grew from the 1960 San Juan NWR plus earlier 1937 island refuges.

events.text: The Eberstadt family donated the 80-acre former estate of New York banker Ferdinand Eberstadt at Lloyd Harbor to the Interior Department in 1967 under the Migratory Bird Conservation Act, creating Target Rock National Wildlife Refuge.

authority.citation: Donation accepted under the Migratory Bird Conservation Act

sources.name: Town of Huntington, NY, Trails Guide: Target Rock (estate of Ferdinand Eberstadt donated to the Interior Department in 1967)
FWS, Target Rock NWR About Us

events.note: Pass A (fws.gov: the Eberstadts donated 80 acres in 1967 through the Migratory Bird Conservation Act) and Pass B (Town of Huntington trail guide: the Eberstadt estate was donated to the Interior Department in 1967) agree on the year and donor. No exact date was found.

events.text: Natalie Peters Webster and her mother, Natalie Wells Peters, donated their roughly 200-acre family estate in Islip, Long Island, to the federal government in 1968 as a sanctuary for birds and other wildlife, which became Seatuck National Wildlife Refuge.

authority.citation: Donation to the Fish and Wildlife Service

sources.name: Seatuck Environmental Association, About Seatuck
FWS, Seatuck NWR page and About Us

events.note: Pass A (fws.gov: acquired in 1968 as a donation from the Peters family) and Pass B (Seatuck Environmental Association: the 200-acre estate was donated in 1968 for an "inviolate sanctuary") agree on the 1968 donation. The association says the property was "eventually" established as a refuge, so the formal designation could postdate the gift; no separate designation date was found.

events.text: The Wassaw Island Trust, formed by the Parsons family, sold Wassaw Island to The Nature Conservancy in 1969, which conveyed it to the federal government as Wassaw National Wildlife Refuge.

authority.citation: Deed from The Nature Conservancy (FWS cites a Deed of Donation dated October 20, 1969)

sources.name: New Georgia Encyclopedia, "Wassaw Island"
FWS, Savannah Coastal Refuges Complex CCP (2011), refuge purposes

events.note: Pass A (2011 CCP: designated a refuge on October 20, 1969, by a Deed of Donation from The Nature Conservancy "for the sum of one dollar") and Pass B (New Georgia Encyclopedia: in 1969 the trust sold the island to the Conservancy for $1 million and the Conservancy then sold it to the federal government for the same amount) agree on 1969 and the route through The Nature Conservancy. They disagree on the price; the exact day, October 20, rests on the FWS source.

events.text: The Campbell Family Foundation gave the Sevilleta land grant ranch to The Nature Conservancy in 1973, which turned it over to the Fish and Wildlife Service as Sevilleta National Wildlife Refuge.

sources.name: New Mexico Magazine, "Sevilleta Wilderness"
FWS, Sevilleta NWR About Us

events.note: Pass A (fws.gov: the Campbell Family Foundation donated the property to The Nature Conservancy in 1973, which donated it to FWS; "On December 28, 1973 Sevilleta National Wildlife Refuge was established") and Pass B (New Mexico Magazine: gifted to The Nature Conservancy in 1973, then turned over to FWS) agree on 1973. The exact day, December 28, rests on the FWS source.

events.name: Coastal Maine National Wildlife Refuge
events.text: The refuge was established in 1966, in cooperation with the State of Maine, as the Coastal Maine National Wildlife Refuge to protect salt marshes and estuaries for migratory birds; it was renamed and dedicated to Rachel Carson on June 27, 1970.

sources.name: Wells National Estuarine Research Reserve blog, "Marking Murky Milestones"
FWS, Rachel Carson NWR About Us

events.note: Pass A (fws.gov: Coastal Maine NWR established December 16, 1966 under the Migratory Bird Conservation Act; renamed and dedicated to Rachel Carson on June 27, 1970) and Pass B (Wells Reserve: the Coastal Maine NWR "was indeed established in 1966"; dedication June 27, 1970) agree on 1966 and the 1970 dedication. The exact day, December 16, rests on the FWS page. fws.gov says "Congress established" it; under the Migratory Bird Conservation Act the approval would normally come from the Migratory Bird Conservation Commission, which includes members of Congress, so the authority is recorded as administrative and should be checked.

events.text: After the Pacific Remote Islands Marine National Monument was proclaimed on January 6, 2009, Secretary of the Interior Order 3284 of January 16, 2009 placed the waters around Wake Atoll under Fish and Wildlife Service management as part of the National Wildlife Refuge System.

authority.citation: Secretary of the Interior Order 3284 (implementing Proclamation 8336)

sources.name: USGS Open-File Report 2023-1066, Biodiversity Surveys of Wake Atoll
FWS ServCat, Establishment Documents: Wake Atoll NWR, Secretarial Order 3284 (16 Jan 2009)

events.note: Pass A (FWS Realty record: SO 3284 of January 16, 2009 directs FWS to manage the lands and waters of Wake out to 12 nautical miles as a unit of the Refuge System) and Pass B (USGS report: on January 16, 2009, through Secretary Order 3284, management was delegated; the Air Force keeps managing the atoll itself under a 1972 agreement; FWS manages the areas from mean low water out to 50 nautical miles as part of the Refuge System) agree on date and order. They differ on the seaward extent (12 vs 50 nautical miles).

wake-atoll-national-wildlife-refuge.note: The atoll's land stays under Air Force management; the refuge covers surrounding waters.

events.text: Pilot Knob National Wildlife Refuge was established in 1987 when the Pilot Knob Ore Company donated the 90-acre summit of Pilot Knob, whose old iron mines shelter wintering Indiana bats, under the Endangered Species Act.

authority.citation: Donation accepted under the Endangered Species Act of 1973

sources.name: FWS, Pilot Knob NWR page and About Us
FWS, Mingo, Pilot Knob and Ozark Cavefish NWRs CCP (2007)

events.note: Pass A (fws.gov: established 1987; Pilot Knob Ore Company donated 90 acres) found only FWS sources. Wikipedia (a lead, not proof) ties the donation to the company ending mining on July 22, 1987. Pass B found no independent record.

events.text: Reelfoot National Wildlife Refuge was established on August 28, 1941, under the Migratory Bird Conservation Act.

sources.name: FWS, Reelfoot and Lake Isom NWRs Comprehensive Conservation Plan (2006)

events.note: Pass A (2006 CCP: established August 28, 1941, under the Migratory Bird Conservation Act) found only an FWS source; no executive order appears in the National Archives disposition table for 1941. Pass B found no independent record (a Tennessee state lease or contemporary newspaper report would settle it).

events.text: Rose Atoll was made a national wildlife refuge on July 15, 1973, by a cooperative agreement between the Government of American Samoa and the Bureau of Sport Fisheries and Wildlife.

authority.citation: Cooperative agreement with the Government of American Samoa

sources.name: FWS, Rose Atoll NWR About Us
Federal Register, Rose Atoll NWR notice of intent to prepare a CCP, 74 FR 57701 (Nov. 9, 2009)
FWS news release, May 13, 1974, "Sooty tern and sea turtle refuge established in Samoan Islands"

events.note: All sources found are FWS-authored: fws.gov gives July 15, 1973; the 2009 Federal Register notice says established in 1973 after a cooperative agreement; a 1974 Interior news release announced it. No American Samoa government or other independent record was found. Separately, President George W. Bush's Proclamation 8337 of January 6, 2009 made the atoll a marine national monument.

events.text: Sachuest Point National Wildlife Refuge began in 1970 with a donation of about 70 acres from the Audubon Society of Rhode Island.

sources.name: FWS, Sachuest Point NWR Comprehensive Conservation Plan (2002)

events.note: Year and donor come from Wikipedia, used only as a lead, and the FWS CCP was not found to state an establishment date in the text searched. Neither pass produced a dated record; needs the CCP history chapter or a 1970 Rhode Island newspaper.

events.text: Sacramento River National Wildlife Refuge was established in 1989 to protect riparian habitat along the Sacramento River between Red Bluff and Princeton.

sources.name: FWS, Sacramento River NWR page
FWS, Sacramento River NWR Final CCP (2005)

events.note: FWS-only sources (fws.gov: established in 1989). The FWS Realty record lists a 1988 act (102 Stat. 1778) authorizing land acquisition, which may relate. No independent record found.

events.text: Saddle Mountain National Wildlife Refuge was created on November 30, 1971, through a permit from the Atomic Energy Commission (now Energy Department) letting the Fish and Wildlife Service manage part of the Hanford Site's Wahluke Slope.

authority.citation: Permit for Management and Recreational Use of the Wahluke Slope (1971), under the Fish and Wildlife Act of 1956

sources.name: FWS, Hanford Reach National Monument Final CCP/EIS (2008), compatibility determinations

events.note: Pass A (2008 CCP: established November 30, 1971, through a permit with the Department of Energy) found only an FWS source. The permit-issuing agency in 1971 was the Atomic Energy Commission; the CCP names its successor. The refuge now lies within Hanford Reach National Monument (Proclamation 7319, June 9, 2000). No independent record of the 1971 permit was found.

events.text: The U.S. Navy transferred Seal Island, a former bombing target off Vinalhaven, Maine, to the Fish and Wildlife Service in 1972 to become Seal Island National Wildlife Refuge.

authority.citation: Wildlife Order 96, under 16 U.S.C. 667b (transfer of surplus federal property for wildlife)

sources.name: FWS ServCat, Establishment Documents: Seal Island NWR, Wildlife Order 96 (11 Aug 1972)
FWS, Maine Coastal Islands NWR Final CCP (2005)

events.note: FWS-only sources: the Realty record (Wildlife Order 96, August 11, 1972, transfer from the Navy) and the 2005 CCP (established 1972 under 16 U.S.C. 667b). No Navy or other independent record found.

events.text: Shiawassee National Wildlife Refuge was established in 1953 near Saginaw, Michigan, to provide habitat for migratory waterfowl.

authority.citation: Migratory Bird Conservation Act (presumed; not verified)

sources.name: FWS, Shiawassee NWR page

events.note: FWS-only source for the year. The establishing authority and exact date were not found; the FWS Realty "refuge purpose" sheet exists in ServCat but was not read in full. Needs a Migratory Bird Conservation Commission report or a 1953 Michigan newspaper.

events.text: Slade National Wildlife Refuge was established in 1941 through a donation of land around Harker Lake in Kidder County, North Dakota, by Northern Pacific Railroad executive George T. Slade.

sources.name: FWS, Slade NWR page

events.note: FWS-only source. Wikipedia (lead only) says Slade gave the land in 1940 and the refuge dates from 1941, so the gift and establishment years may differ. No executive order for Slade appears in the National Archives disposition tables for 1940-1941.

events.text: Stone Lakes National Wildlife Refuge, south of Sacramento, was officially established in 1994 with the acquisition of its first property, becoming the 505th unit of the National Wildlife Refuge System.

sources.name: FWS, Stone Lakes NWR page
FWS, Stone Lakes NWR Comprehensive Conservation Plan (2007)

events.note: FWS-only sources, and they are not fully consistent: fws.gov and the CCP introduction say established in 1994 (first acquisition), while another CCP passage says the Service "established the Refuge in 1992," which likely refers to approval of the acquisition boundary. No independent record found.

events.text: Sutter National Wildlife Refuge was established in 1945 in the Sutter Bypass as a refuge and breeding ground for migratory birds and to reduce waterfowl damage to crops.

authority.citation: Migratory Bird Conservation Act (presumed; later acquisitions under the Lea Act of 1948)

sources.name: FWS, Sacramento, Delevan, Colusa and Sutter NWRs Final CCP (2009)
FWS, Sutter NWR page

events.note: FWS-only sources for 1945. The FWS Realty file cites the Lea Act of May 18, 1948 (62 Stat. 238), which postdates 1945, so the founding authority is unclear. No independent record found.

events.text: Tallahatchie National Wildlife Refuge in northern Mississippi was established in March 1991 under the Migratory Bird Conservation Act and the Consolidated Farm and Rural Development Act, largely from former Farmers Home Administration lands.

authority.citation: Migratory Bird Conservation Act; Consolidated Farm and Rural Development Act

sources.name: FWS, Tallahatchie NWR Hunt Plan, EA and Compatibility Determination (2020)
FWS, Tallahatchie NWR page

events.note: FWS-only sources (hunt plan: established March 1991; fws.gov: 1991). No independent record found.

events.text: Texas Point National Wildlife Refuge, near Sabine Pass on the upper Texas coast, was established in 1979.

sources.name: FWS, McFaddin and Texas Point NWRs brochure

events.note: Only the FWS brochure gives a year ("Established in 1980 and 1979, McFaddin NWR and Texas Point NWR"). No establishing document, authority or exact date was found, and no independent record.

events.text: Toppenish National Wildlife Refuge in Washington's Yakima Valley was established in 1964 with the purchase of the 40-acre Cloe Tract, after the Migratory Bird Conservation Commission authorized it on August 21, 1962.

authority.citation: Migratory Bird Conservation Commission approval (Aug. 21, 1962); first purchase 1964

sources.name: FWS, Toppenish NWR Inventory and Monitoring Plan (2020)

events.note: FWS-only source. A Migratory Bird Conservation Commission annual report for 1962-1963 would give an independent check of the approval date.

events.text: Trustom Pond National Wildlife Refuge in South Kingstown, Rhode Island, began in 1974 with land donated by Ann Kenyon Morse; the Audubon Society of Rhode Island added 151 acres in 1982.

sources.name: FWS, Trustom Pond NWR About Us
FWS, Trustom Pond NWR Comprehensive Conservation Plan (2002)

events.note: The 1974 date and the Morse donation come from leads (Wikipedia) and were not found in the FWS text searched; fws.gov confirms only the 1982 Audubon donation. Neither pass produced a dated record of establishment. Needs the CCP history section or a Rhode Island source.

events.text: Two Ponds National Wildlife Refuge, a 72-acre urban refuge in Arvada, Colorado, was established in 1992.

sources.name: FWS, Two Ponds NWR general brochure

events.note: Only the FWS brochure gives a year ("Established in 1992"). The establishing action and authority were not found, and there is no independent record yet.

events.text: Wallops Island National Wildlife Refuge was created when NASA's Wallops Flight Center transferred 373 acres of salt marsh and woodland on the Virginia mainland to the Fish and Wildlife Service.

sources.name: FWS, Chincoteague and Wallops Island NWRs Comprehensive Conservation Plan (2015), sec. 1.5.2
FWS, Wallops Island NWR page

events.note: The FWS sources disagree: the 2015 CCP says created March 11, 1971, when 373 acres were transferred from NASA; fws.gov says 343 acres were set aside in 1975; Wikipedia (lead only) says July 10, 1975. No NASA or other independent record was found to settle the date. The CCP date is shown but should not be published until confirmed.

wallops-island-national-wildlife-refuge.note: Establishment date conflicts between FWS sources (1971 vs 1975).
